page: Microsoft Azure D2alds_v7 is a low-memory variant within the general-purpose Daldsv7 instance family, running on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. Powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at up to 4.5 GHz, the instance allocates 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from a single physical core with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU cache architecture comprises 48 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and a shared 32 MB L3 cache. It incorporates hardware instruction support for AVX-512, AVX-VNNI, SHA-NI, and AES encryption. Memory is configured at 4.0 GB, yielding a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio. The instance includes 118 GB of fast local NVMe SSD storage, while discrete GPU hardware is omitted.

Performance benchmarks highlight significant single-threaded speed contrasted with constrained total capacity. In single-core stress-ng tests, the EPYC 9V45 reaches top-tier results, a strength further demonstrated by upper-decile throughput in single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. Large-block memory bandwidth benchmarks register middle-tier read and write rates. Conversely, aggregate multi-core throughput across stress-ng, PassMark CPU tests, and database transactions settles in lower performance tiers due to the dual-thread ceiling. Similarly, redis operations and static web serving throughput reflect the hardware constraints of 2 vCPUs and 4 GB of RAM.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the D2alds_v7 provides access to modern high-frequency AMD server silicon and local NVMe storage without requiring expenditure on unneeded RAM. This makes the instance economically practical for compute workloads that rely heavily on single-thread clock speed rather than massive concurrency or memory depth. Optimal deployment scenarios include small-scale web serving, CI/CD build agents, single-threaded batch processing, lightweight microservices, and development environments where bundled NVMe disk performance provides fast local scratch space.
description: Microsoft Azure D2alds_v7 is a compact general-purpose virtual machine equipped with an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor delivering dedicated compute across 2 vCPUs from a single physical core at clock speeds up to 4.5 GHz. The configuration provides 4.0 GB of memory alongside an integrated 118 GB local NVMe SSD, but excludes discrete GPU acceleration. Benefiting from modern Zen architecture features including AVX-512 extensions and 32 MB of L3 cache, the instance demonstrates exceptional single-core performance, ranking in the top tier for single-threaded tasks such as gzip compression and bzip3 decompression. However, due to its low memory footprint and two-thread constraint, multi-core aggregate throughput and database operations remain limited. Offering an economical entry point for high-clock requirements without excessive RAM overhead, the D2alds_v7 is suitable for lightweight web serving, continuous integration runners, batch data compression, and basic application hosting.
